QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_43

question.text: Arranged from STRONGEST to WEAKEST causal inference, which order is correct?

answer.text: RCT > Quasi-experimental (DiD, PSM) > Pre-post with comparison > Pre-post single-group > Anecdote

explanation.text: The Logic: The standard evidence-hierarchy for causal inference is: Randomised Controlled Trials (strongest) > Quasi-experimental methods (DiD, RDD, PSM, synthetic control) > Pre-post with comparison group > Pre-post single-group > Cross-sectional/anecdotal (weakest). Stronger designs better isolate the causal effect of an intervention from confounding factors. The Trap: Options A and C reverse the hierarchy and place anecdote/self-assessment above RCTs. Option D mixes incompatible constructs — SROI is a monetisation method, not a causal-inference design. Note: This specific causal-inference evidence hierarchy (RCT, DiD, PSM, quasi-experimental versus pre-post versus anecdote) is not laid out in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) at pages 8, 134, 151-152 or in full-text search. The framing above reflects general industry/development-evaluation knowledge of evidence hierarchies.
